definitions.B_INTRODUCTION_VS_NEXUS: an accepted recommendation introduces a catastrophe relative to frozen effective Nexus-else-S0
definitions.C_UNION_INTRODUCTION: an accepted class triggers A or B or both; counted once (primary endpoint)
definitions.SELECTIVE_FAILURE_RATE: unique accepted introduction classes / accepted classes
definitions.FULL_POPULATION_INTRODUCTION_RATE: unique accepted introduction classes / all eligible classes
definitions.notTheSameAs: the risk model's catastrophe label (catastrophic in at least one member world). An introduction additionally requires the comparator not to be catastrophic in that member world.
definitions.abstention: no recommendation; never a safe native-world outcome; what happens next is outside the kernel

pooledDescriptive.label: POST_HOC_EXPLORATORY_ONLY
pooledDescriptive.note: out-of-fold development plus historical validation. Different models (fold models vs the frozen model) and a spent population: descriptive only, not a test.

sampleSize.assumption: exact one-sided binomial test of H0: rate >= 0.01; independent decisions; multiply by the design effect and divide by coverage to get eligible classes
sampleSize.simultaneousClaims: One claim on the UNION endpoint at 95% bounds both comparator endpoints, because each comparator event is a subset of the union. Separate comparator claims (for example on exposure-adjusted denominators) need 97.5% each.

scaleReference.source: SK1_RESULT.md: 26 blocks screened, 2,298 admitted, 600 validation classes

discriminationHypothesisPairedDesign.note: top-1 unsafe rate = forced-choice union introduction rate at full coverage; baseline is the frozen SK1 figure on historical validation, used as a planning value only
discriminationHypothesisPairedDesign.assumption: independent failures between the two policies (conservative: positively associated failures need fewer classes)

resubstitution.note: the same frozen threshold, three readings of the same 1,000 exploration classes
resubstitution.reading: In-sample acceptance is larger and cleaner than out-of-fold acceptance of the same classes. Any acceptance rule must be judged on classes its model never saw.

thresholdSelection.note: the frozen threshold was itself picked from a grid by its out-of-fold rate
thresholdSelection.consequence: the out-of-fold rate at the chosen point is a minimum over eligible grid points and is mildly optimistic; validation (0.66%) did not contradict it

failureFreePrefix.label: POST_HOC_EXPLORATORY_ONLY
failureFreePrefix.note: a cutoff placed just before the first observed failure is chosen by the outcome and carries no valid zero-event bound

riskCoverage.label: POST_HOC_EXPLORATORY_ONLY
riskCoverage.warning: No point on any curve is a qualified or proposed operating point. The only acceptance rule ever applied is the frozen bound <= 0.2.

horizon.H0_H2_variation: NOT_ESTIMABLE: every exploration and validation class is H2 by construction of the SK1 schedule

distributionShift.note: Validation families are disjoint from exploration families by design, so validation is family-out-of-distribution. Shift indicators are score-level; no per-feature shift test was run.

definitions.WITHIN_MENU_RISK_ORDERING_ERROR: a failing forced choice where no safe alternative has a lower risk bound than the chosen action: the risk order of the menu is itself wrong
definitions.RANKING_CONTRACT_ERROR: a failing forced choice where some safe alternative has a lower bound (necessarily in the same tier) and lost on the expected-regret order
definitions.RISK_ESTIMATION_ERROR: systematic miscalibration of the catastrophe estimate across menus
definitions.ABSTENTION_DECISION_ERROR: accepting a class whose forced choice fails (false accept), or withholding a forced choice with no observed introduction (false abstain)
definitions.safeAlternative: a selectable action outside the chosen set that introduces against neither comparator in any sampled member world

withinMenu.note: Does the estimate order the actions of ONE menu? Label "catastrophe" is what the model was fit on; label "introduction" is the gated event.

riskEstimationError.evidence: frozen run: expected calibration error 0.026 on 5,304 validation action estimates; conservative for selected actions (SK1.1). That calibration is on catastrophe, not on introduction.

displacementActionsByDirection_outOfBag.note: MOVE and RETREAT actions on exploration, out-of-bag estimate against observed labels. A subgroup whose observed rate exceeds its mean estimate is under-estimated.

featureCollisions.note: actions of one menu with IDENTICAL 144-feature rows. The featurisation cannot separate them, whatever is learned from it.

crossClass.note: identical 144-feature rows that occur in more than one class

for: a safe action exists in every exploration and every validation class
the frozen estimate orders actions within a menu well above chance on classes it never saw
in almost every failing class the chosen action and the best safe alternative differ in public features
against: existence of a safe action is evaluator knowledge, not public knowledge
ordering errors are unanimous or near-unanimous across bags, so more resampling of the same learner on the same features would not correct them
a small number of menus contain actions the featurisation cannot tell apart yet have different outcomes
PUBLIC_SAFE_ACTION_IDENTIFIABILITY.whatWouldSettleIt: a prospective test of a learner built for within-menu discrimination, on fresh family-disjoint classes; nothing in existing evidence can

verdicts.pointEstimateBasis: out-of-fold development and historical validation both show a point rate below 1% at coverage above 40% for the frozen rule; the pessimistic out-of-bag diagnostic does not

practicalityRule.rule: feasible only if an existing reading already supports the bound at the coverage target, or the eligible validation classes needed for 80% power at the planning rate do not exceed the practical ceiling
practicalityRule.ceilingBasis: five times the SK1 validation population, more than SK1 admitted in total (2,298); a disclosed planning assumption

verdicts.classificationScope: for the frozen SK1 policy, against the research targets 1% / 95% / 40%, at practical DEV sample sizes
verdicts.priorityRule: discrimination is recommended when the bound is not practically feasible and within-menu ordering errors are the majority of failing forced choices on both historical validation and out-of-bag exploration
